solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Awfully mean bachelor cracks beer open

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of mean are put out of order
the bachelor letter cracks the beer word by getting inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A grumpy single man forces his way into the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' here means receptive to ideas, not unsealed like a bottle, despite the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is receptive and willing to be persuaded, i.e. open to suggestion.

clue.text: Country club put on one extravaganza at last

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
to don clothes is to put them on
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of extravaganza

explanation.surface: A social club stages one last lavish show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society but is the weapon MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: North Macedonia, long called Macedonia, is a Balkan nation.

clue.text: Opera singer Jessye, without second name?

indicators.note: without second says the later of the two matching letters in her surname is dropped

parts.note: Jessye Norman was a celebrated American soprano

explanation.surface: A question about an opera star known only by her first name.
explanation.walkthrough: Jessye Norman's surname has two Ns; 'without second' drops the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's famous opera about a druid priestess.

clue.text: I'm not playing with band — it entails a racket!

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to play with a noisy band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' seems to mean noise from the band, but it is the sporting bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a sport played with a racket and shuttlecock.

clue.text: Old Cockney's stopped getting high

parts.note: ex- means former, old

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, traditionally drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: halted means stopped

explanation.surface: An elderly East Ender has quit taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney's' signals the dropped H: HALTED becomes ALTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Exalted means of lofty rank or status, elevated.

clue.text: Officer in charge consumed by passion for stripper?

indicators.note: consumed by says the officer letters are swallowed inside the passion word

parts.note: lust is strong passion
OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding, officer in charge

explanation.surface: A senior officer is overwhelmed by desire for an exotic dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripper' suggests a striptease artist, but locusts strip fields bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarms of these insects strip crops and vegetation entirely, hence the cryptic label.

clue.text: Drop in around one, having climbed tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards
around says the visit word goes round the numeral

parts.note: to call is to drop in on someone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone visits at about one o'clock after climbing a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts I inside CALL to make CALIL; 'having climbed' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a flowering shrub or small tree of the olive family.

clue.text: Cast has lyric soprano as potential Butterfly?

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters are thrown and moulded anew

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: An opera cast includes a lyric soprano who might sing Madama Butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' rearranges HASLYRICS. 'Butterfly' points to Puccini's opera, but means the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa in its case is a future butterfly, not yet emerged as an adult insect.

clue.text: Investment is, in recession, regularly meagre

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the word is is read backwards
regularly picks every other letter of meagre

explanation.surface: An economist warns that investment is thin during a recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial, but an old sense means besieging a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town is to surround it militarily, so investment is a blockade.

clue.text: Heartlessly scrubbed and scratched

indicators.note: heartlessly means losing the central letter of the scrubbing word

parts.note: scoured means scrubbed hard

explanation.surface: Someone cleaned a surface so harshly it was marked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes U, the middle letter of SCOURED.
explanation.definitionFit: Scored means marked with cuts or lines, as when a surface is scratched.

clue.text: Everyone turned green, finding a harmful substance

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: turned suggests the letters of green are twisted around

explanation.surface: Everybody went pale green on discovering something poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' rearranges GREEN to ERGEN; 'turned green' looks like feeling sick.
explanation.definitionFit: This is any substance that triggers an allergic reaction in the body.

clue.text: One is securing trade with credit, mostly? That's impractical

indicators.note: securing says the first two words hold the business word between them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is a trade

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the credit word is dropped

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that closing a deal largely on credit is sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims TICK to TIC. Buying 'on tick' is British for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idealistic pursues lofty principles over workable realities, so is unrealistic.

clue.text: The woman had to get rid of outhouse

definitions.meaning: to discard, as a snake does its skin
a small hut in the garden

explanation.surface: A woman had to clear out her garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: the contraction she'd, to cast off, and a garden hut.

clue.text: Popular detective faces court charge

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A well-loved police detective appears before a judge on a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict is to formally accuse someone of a crime, i.e. charge them.

clue.text: I can hold forth about European travelling

indicators.note: about, in the sense of on the subject of, lets the ranting follow the European it concerns

parts.note: a tin is a can
to rant is to hold forth at length

explanation.surface: A speaker boasts of being able to lecture on Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is read as 'on the subject of': the RANT comes after the E it concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant describes someone who moves from place to place, a wanderer.

clue.text: Unaffected by time without a romantic partner?

definitions.meaning: timeless, never going out of date
having no date, nobody to go out with

explanation.surface: Someone ageless yet single.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: ageless or eternal, and with no partner for an evening out.

clue.text: One persecutes soldiers surrounded by hills

indicators.note: surrounded by says the soldiers sit between the hills

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, so two of them give the hills
men are soldiers

explanation.surface: A persecutor hounds troops trapped among the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is a person who harasses or inflicts suffering on another.

clue.text: Jet carries one above cloud, finally — that's high

indicators.note: carries says the jet word holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a spout is a jet of liquid

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the card before the next piece

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of cloud

explanation.surface: A jet aircraft lifts someone above the clouds, really high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' seems an aircraft but is SPOUT, a jet of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced out is slang for dazed or intoxicated, as if on drugs.

clue.text: Job's virtue is time in peace, working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A proverbial virtue is defined as time spent quietly at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The Book of Job's hero is famed for patient suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Job's proverbial quality was enduring hardship without complaint, i.e. forbearance.

clue.text: Wandering sailor turns up in Morecambe?

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the comedian's name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian of Morecambe and Wise

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the sailor word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman drifts into the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morecambe' looks like the Lancashire town but stands for comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means straying from a regular course, irregular and unpredictable.

clue.text: Contributor to misbehaviour, a scallywag?

indicators.note: a contributor gives only a part, so the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A scamp is blamed for playing a part in some naughtiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous scamp who causes trouble, much like a scallywag.

clue.text: Long article by revolutionary

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece written by a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn for it intensely.

clue.text: Sigh for Conservative Party

parts.note: a rave is a wild party

explanation.surface: Someone pines for the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: To sigh for something is to long for it, which is to desire it badly.

clue.text: Football's governing body gagged entertaining fellow? Unlikely

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football

indicators.note: entertaining says the retching word hosts the fellow inside it

parts.note: retched means gagged

explanation.surface: Football's officials felt sick at the thought of entertaining someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gagged' suggests silenced, but means retched.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-fetched describes something improbable or hard to believe.

clue.text: Heard someone cooking chips, perhaps for brother

indicators.note: heard says the word is to be listened to, not read

parts.note: a fryer is one who fries food such as chips

explanation.surface: A monk overhears someone at a chip shop fryer.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips are British for thick-cut fries.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a religious order, addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Rate fell below 100

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the skin word under the numeral

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
a fell is an animal hide or skin

explanation.surface: A rate of something dropped under a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' looks like a number but is the verb to scold; 'fell' is the noun, a pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone, in an old sense, is to scold them angrily.

clue.text: One resigned to destiny of overweight top celebs

parts.note: fat means overweight
the A-list is the group of top celebrities

explanation.surface: Plump top celebrities accept that fate has the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist believes all events are predetermined and accepts them.

clue.text: Turkey possesses crude oil after a fashion

indicators.note: possesses says the country code holds the other letters inside

parts.note: TR is Turkey's international vehicle code

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters of oil are put in rough order

explanation.surface: Turkey holds unrefined oil, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a fashion' looks like a phrase; 'fashion' alone, a verb, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to shape or adapt it to fit, i.e. to fashion it.

clue.text: A fool to scoff sandwiches fast? Not half

indicators.note: sandwiches says the mocking word encloses the other piece

parts.note: to jeer is to scoff

indicators.note: not half means only one half of the word fast survives

explanation.surface: A silly person wolfs down sandwiches quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' suggests eating, but means mock; 'Not half' drops FA from FAST to leave ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester was a court fool employed to entertain.

clue.text: Old soldier heading for trouble aboard key warship

indicators.note: aboard says the other pieces go on inside the key word

parts.note: core means key, central
a vet is a veteran, an old soldier

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of trouble

explanation.surface: A veteran heading for trouble boards a crucial warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small, fast naval escort vessel.
